1890.s: I must try and recall them, grasp the elusive ghosts which were tonight pattering around me on noiseless, shadowy feet, and vanishing when I strove to stay them, by catching their impalpable hands, or floating misty garments.
1890.au: The reveries of a spinster. | $c: By Helen Davies.

1900.s: "Helga's dreams always come to pass, you know," said the man of the elusive sweater half banteringly.
1900.au: The flying death / | $c: by Samuel Hopkins Adams ... ; illustrated by C.R. Macauley.

1900.s: Pale blue, her gown was, of an elusive and impossible fabric that swathed her like a cloud.
1900.au: The woman that's good; | a story of the undoing of a dreamer.

1910.s: Various elderly gentlemen began adjusting earmuffs and mufflers, and spearing with their arms at elusive sleeve openings.
1910.au: Old Judge Priest, | $c: by Irvin S. Cobb.

1910.s: …the cheers certain vocal explosions up and down the whole chromatic scale which, swelling in volume, finally swallowed up all other sounds, and frantic hands were seen through the windows clutching at elusive coat tail pockets.
She remembered being lifted from the pillow on the car seat, and hugged and kissed, and having her limp, sleepy arms thrust into elusive coat sleeves.
1910.au: Miss Santa Claus of the Pullman / | $c: by Annie Fellows Johnson [i.e. Johnston] ; with illustrations by Reginald B. Birch.

1910.s: Then she had been embarrassed because she had strayed into his room while he was dressing, emerging triumphantly from his closet, in fact, with that elusive new shirt. . . .
1910.au: The wine of astonishment, | $c: by Mary Hastings Bradley ...

1910.s: …where a statuesque queenly looking woman gazed languidly about in frank boredom, while a lanky youth with flushed, beardless face and too bright eyes leaned far over the table and tried to take her elusive, gloved hand in his.
1910.au: The primal law, | $c: by Isabel Ostrander.

1920.s: And Molly, being a girl, slipped her hand through my arm and cried a little and laughed a little as we watched Jim's dark head pursuing the elusive scarlet cap in front of him.

But the effect was not pleasing even then — so he placed it in his pocket, taking a red handkerchief from his other pocket, and laying it carefully over the elusive pipe, to anchor it — if that were possible.
1920.au: Purple springs / | $c: by Nellie L. McClung.

1920.s: An unceasing necessity for chatter, chatter of the right kind; carriage numbers to attend to; tickets to be produced from an elusive waistcoat pocket.
